observations.body: When opponents accuse Jesus of making himself God, he cites the line “I said, you are gods,” asks how Scripture addresses those who received God’s word, and returns attention to his works and relation to the Father.
observations.label: Scripture posture

payload.posture: Read “Jesus cites “you are gods” in an accusation of blasphemy” as its own Scripture scene before carrying its imagery into another heavenly gathering.
payload.tension: the passage shows Psalm 82’s gods-language carried into a dispute about Jesus’ words and works, while John quotes one line without resolving every identity in Psalm 82 or making the quoted addressees identical with Jesus.
